target.name: bbwebsocket
target.address_convention: image_addr = listing_addr - 0x100000; every addr below is an image addr
target.line_convention: Lnnnnn = global line number in the decompiled listing

claims.statement: WSConn::accept registers a pattern wait for the 4 bytes '\r\n\r\n' and the callback argument is the INDEX of that pattern inside the receive buffer (ptr-buf), not a length.

rodata.note: merged into the tail of the 19-byte 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\n\r\n' literal at 0x1f6bd

claims.statement: After a successful upgrade the server drops exactly idx+4 bytes from the front of the receive buffer, so bytes pipelined behind the header are preserved.
The server finds the key with memmem over the WHOLE buffer for the 19-byte literal 'Sec-WebSocket-Key: ' (trailing space included); it is not line-anchored and is case-sensitive.
claims.test: test_server_handshake/key header not on first line

claims.statement: The key value is copied verbatim (no trim, no base64 validation) from p+19 until CR or LF, bounded by the buffer end and by a hard cap of 127 bytes.
accept = base64(SHA1(key_bytes || GUID)) where GUID is the 36-byte ASCII '258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11'; the message length fed to SHA-1 is strlen(key)+0x24.

evidence.insn: mov QWORD PTR [rax],rdi  (GUID appended right after key)

rodata.note: GUID is NOT in .rodata; it is built from 5 movabs immediates

claims.statement: SHA-1 is standard FIPS 180-1: IV 67452301/EFCDAB89/98BADCFE/10325476/C3D2E1F0, 80 rounds with constants 5A827999/6ED9EBA1/8F1BBCDC/CA62C1D6, big-endian message words, 0x80 padding, 8-byte big-endian bit length; digest is 20 bytes.

evidence.what: FUN_0010d620 = SHA-1 block transform (1430 pseudocode lines)

evidence.insn: movdqu xmm4,[rdi+0x1c]  (block at +0x1c; h[5] at +0, bitlen at +0x14, fill at +0x5c)

evidence.detail: 0x80 pad, zero pad to 56 mod 64, 8-byte big-endian bit length

claims.statement: Base64 uses alphabet 'A-Za-z0-9+/=' (index 64 = '='), emits 4 chars per 3 bytes and '==' for a 1-byte tail; base64 of the 20-byte digest is 28 chars.

evidence.insn: mov BYTE PTR [rsp+0xb0],cl ; movzx ecx,[rsi+rcx] (table lookup, 4 per group)

claims.statement: If the key header is present with a non-empty value the server ALWAYS replies 101; it never validates Upgrade, Connection, Sec-WebSocket-Version or the request line (none of those strings exist in .rodata).

evidence.detail: end of base64 loop: 'if (0x13 < iVar31) goto LAB_001138c0' jumps straight to the 101 builder, skipping the GET check
only permessage-deflate and accept string are consulted

claims.statement: The 101 response is the .rodata 0x1f7a8 template; its first %s is the 46-byte extensions line (.rodata 0x1f778) when permessage-deflate was negotiated, otherwise the empty string at .rodata 0x1f6d0; the second %s is the accept value.

permessage-deflate is 'negotiated' if the 18-byte token appears ANYWHERE in the receive buffer (including pipelined frame bytes); it sets this+0x58=1 and initialises inflateInit2_(z, -15, "1.2.7", 0x70) / deflateInit2_(z, -1, 8, -15, 8, 0, "1.2.7", 0x70).

evidence.insn: mov edi,0x70 ; operator new(0x70) for the inflate z_stream at this+0x60

claims.statement: Without a non-empty key the request-line branch runs: it requires n>5, buf[0..4]=='GET /' and buf[5]!='/'; then it replies the 19-byte 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\n\r\n' and hands the path (buf[5..] up to ' '/CR/LF, cleared to empty if two consecutive '.' are seen) to the second callback.

evidence.insn: repz cmps BYTE PTR [rsi],BYTE PTR [rdi] (5 bytes)

claims.statement: For any other request (not 'GET /<non-slash>', no key) the server emits ZERO bytes and replaces the receive handler with TcpConn::discard, i.e. all further input is swallowed.
The client Sec-WebSocket-Key is a constant: base64(16 zero bytes) = 'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=='. The 16-byte buffer is zeroed and there is no rand/time call in the key generation.

evidence.insn: the ONLY call between 0x122b0 and 0x12351 is operator new

claims.statement: The client request is the fixed 155-byte template at .rodata 0x1f6d8 with the key substituted for %s; it always offers permessage-deflate and Version 13.

connect() installs FUN_0010fc40 as the TcpConn data handler; that handler waits for the 4 bytes CRLFCRLF with recv_pat, and its pattern callback FUN_0010dbc0 (1) memmem's the whole buffer for 'permessage-deflate' (18 bytes) to enable this+0x58 and init inflate/deflate, (2) drops idx+4 bytes from the receive buffer, then (3) invokes the captured std::function (the user's on-connect callback).

evidence.insn: mov QWORD PTR [rbx+0x80],rdi  (install as the data callback)

evidence.detail: memmem, set +0x58, drop param_2+4 bytes, invoke param_1[4]

claims.statement: The client never validates the server handshake: neither FUN_0010fc40 nor FUN_0010dbc0 compares the status line, Upgrade, Connection or Sec-WebSocket-Accept. Any response that ends with CRLFCRLF is treated as a successful handshake (its header is dropped and on-connect fires), including 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request' or a wrong Accept value.

evidence.what: FUN_0010dbc0 (pattern callback), full body L11842-L11912: the only string operation is the memmem at 0xdbf4

evidence.detail: no comparison of the response text anywhere

claims.statement: byte0: bit7=FIN, bit6=RSV1, bit5=RSV2 (ignored), bit4=RSV3 (ignored), bits3..0=opcode (masked with 0x0f).
byte1: bit7=MASK, bits6..0=payload-len7 (masked with 0x7f). The MASK bit does not contribute to the length.
payload-len7 <= 125: payload length = len7, header is 2 bytes, and the parser requires exactly 2 buffered bytes before stripping the header.
payload-len7 == 0x7e: the next 2 bytes are read BIG-ENDIAN as the payload length, header is 4 bytes, and the parser waits for 4 buffered bytes in total.

payload-len7 == 0x7f: bytes b2..b5 must all be zero (otherwise WSConn::exit() is called and the connection is torn down), and the length is b6..b9 big-endian reinterpreted as a SIGNED 32-bit value; header is 10 bytes, parser waits for 10 buffered bytes.
The frame header is consumed (memmove'd out of the receive buffer) as soon as it is complete, before any payload byte arrives.

evidence.insn: add r8,rax ; mov QWORD PTR [r14+0x8],r8 (new end after stripping 2)

claims.statement: There is no minimal-length-encoding check: a 126 (0x7e) extended length carrying 0x007e is accepted and yields 126; likewise 0x7f may carry a value < 65536.

evidence.insn: no comparison of the decoded value against 126/0xffff

claims.statement: The MASK bit is not validated against the connection role: masked and unmasked frames are both accepted by the same code path.
For a masked frame the 4-byte mask key sits immediately after the (already stripped) header, i.e. at offset 0 of the remaining buffer; it is read once as a 32-bit value.

evidence.insn: L13958 local_68[0] = *__dest (4 bytes at buffer start)

claims.statement: Unmasking is byte-wise (not a word-wise XOR): msg[old+i] = buf[4+i] ^ mask[i & 3], with i restarting at 0 for every frame, where old is the message-buffer size before this frame.

Timing: the message buffer is first zero-extended by payload_len, then XOR-filled from the receive buffer; afterwards payload_len+4 bytes are removed. The masked path waits for payload_len+4 buffered bytes, the unmasked path only payload_len.
opcode 8 with FIN=1 invokes the user callback with an EMPTY unique_ptr; the close code and reason are never parsed (the payload is still appended to the message buffer and then discarded).

evidence.insn: mov QWORD PTR [rsp+0x20],0x0 (null buffer) ; call rax

claims.statement: opcode 9 (ping) and 0xA (pong) are consumed silently: no pong is generated, no event is delivered, and the connection state is unchanged.

The library never emits Close/Ping/Pong frames: the only frame builder is WSConn::send and its first byte is 0x81 or 0xC1; WSConn::exit clears the pending send buffer and schedules teardown without sending anything.
Control-frame constraints are not validated: a ping/pong/close frame with FIN=0 is treated as the first fragment of a message, and control payloads longer than 125 bytes are accepted.

evidence.insn: cmp BYTE PTR [rbx+0x10],0x0  (FIN check happens first, opcode-agnostic)

evidence.detail: if (FIN==0) read_head() before any opcode inspection

claims.statement: FIN=0 causes the parser to re-enter read_head immediately, appending the frame payload to the message buffer at this+0x48 in arrival order.

On FIN=1 the dispatch uses the opcode of THAT (last) frame, read from the read_data lambda slot +0x14: only 1 (deliver message) and 8 (deliver null) produce an event; 0x0/0x2/others cause the accumulated bytes to be dropped without a callback.

Consequence: the standard text fragmentation sequence 0x01 (FIN=0) + 0x80 (FIN=1, opcode=0) is NEVER delivered, because the final frame's opcode is 0. Only a non-conformant sequence whose final frame carries opcode 1 delivers the concatenation.

evidence.insn: opcode taken from the frame that has FIN=1

evidence.detail: cmp against 1 fails for a continuation frame

claims.statement: recv_more(n) invokes its callback synchronously when the receive buffer already holds >= n bytes, otherwise it stores the continuation in the event loop and re-runs it when more data arrives.
Incoming data is appended to the vector at this+0x40 and then the pattern wait is re-armed; an empty Buffer (peer closed) triggers WSConn::exit().
There is no explicit parser state machine: every data arrival re-parses from the head of the receive buffer, so a partial frame leaves the buffer untouched until all required bytes are present.

evidence.what: frame parser always starts at buf[0]

claims.statement: Consumption compacts the buffer with memmove and keeps the remaining bytes, so multiple pipelined frames and frames split across TCP reads both work; nothing is dropped except the bytes actually consumed.

Inbound permessage-deflate appends 00 00 FF FF to the message, calls inflate with Z_NO_FLUSH into a 0x4000-byte chunk buffer, and treats Z_MEM_ERROR/Z_DATA_ERROR/Z_STREAM_ERROR/Z_NEED_DICT (codes -4,-3,-2,2) as failure, in which case nothing is delivered.
Outbound permessage-deflate uses deflate(z, Z_FINISH=2), then shortens the payload by exactly 4 bytes (the 00 00 FF FF tail) and sets RSV1 in the frame's first byte (0xC1).
RSV1 is sticky per connection (this+0x59): set by any frame header carrying 0x40, cleared only by WSConn::recv, and compression is attempted only when this+0x58 (negotiated) is also set.

WSConn::send builds a single unfragmented text frame: byte0=0x81 (or 0xC1 when compressed), byte1 has MASK=0 and the 7-bit length; length > 125 uses 0x7E + 2 big-endian bytes and length >= 0xFFFF uses 0x7F + four 0x00 bytes + 4 big-endian bytes (strict < 0xffff compare, so 65535 takes the 64-bit branch).

evidence.insn: mov BYTE PTR [rsp+0x20],0x7f ; 0x152c0..0x152f8 four 0x00 ; 0x15307 len>>24 ; 0x15314 len>>16
mov BYTE PTR [rsp+0x20],r15b (low byte, MASK bit stays 0) ; 0x14ea8 _M_range_insert(payload)

unknowns.statement: The final teardown of WSConn::exit (0xc110) is not traced: the tail only installs a lambda into the event loop (PTR__M_invoke_00324fd0, L10042-L10061). Whether/when TcpConn issues shutdown()/close() on the socket is not established, so the TCP-level FIN timing behind a received Close is unknown.
unknowns.blocked_on: TcpConn::exit / EventLoop2::del paths (0x16b80, 0x1a290) were not decompiled in detail

The '

' literal used by both handshake waiters is at 0x1f6cc - it is the tail of the 19-byte 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK

A second, standalone copy of the deflate-negotiation + header-drop logic exists at FUN_0010dbc0 (0xdbc0); 0x12b60 contains the inlined copy (0x138d6..0x139a4). The client path uses the standalone one.
